# Featured Papers

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Differential roles for the spindle assembly checkpoint in error surveillance and mitotic timing](<https://doi.org/10.1038/s44318-026-00931-9>)
*Ryan K Kim, Kuan-Chung Su, Mary-Jane Tsang, Nolan K Maier, Brittania Moodie, Iain M Cheeseman* <br>
Mitotic timing is regulated by an overlapping network of Mad2-mediated APC/C inhibition, Cdk1-dependent Cdc20 phosphorylation, and overall Cdc20 protein levels, rendering Mad2 dispensable for viability in checkpoint-deficient cells.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Midzone bundles of the mammalian anaphase spindle are mechanically coupled both locally and globally](<https://doi.org/10.1083/jcb.202604150>)
*Zachary Mullin-Bernstein, Sterre van Wierst, Carly Garrison, Nathan H. Cho, Sophie Dumont* <br>
PRC1-dependent force transmission causes the anaphase spindle to act as a unified mechanical structure that resists transient perturbations through strong bundle anchorage while dynamically remodeling over longer timescales to segregate chromosomes.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Spatial Control of Compressible Active Fluids](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30092v1>)
*Yu-Chuan Cheng, Dimitris Krommydas, Seungwoo Shin, Paarth Gulati, Michael F. Hagan, Aparna Baskaran, Cristina M. Marchetti, Zvonimir Dogic* <br>
Wavelength-dependent active vortices dictate density modulations in microtubule-based active fluids under patterned activity, demonstrating that controlling chaotic dynamics requires a model incorporating both active stress and isotropic active pressure.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [APLNR regulates directed migration to spatially pattern mesoderm in human gastruloids](<https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.19.760207>)
*Amanda Brooke Johnson, Shailaja Seetharaman, LiAng Yao, Alex Plum, Zhiyuan Yu, Mattia Serra, Idse Heemskerk, Margaret L. Gardel* <br>
Epithelial APELA ligands provide a chemotactic gradient that steers mesodermal progenitors through directional bias rather than increased speed, positioning lineage-competent cells to properly establish local signaling programs and central FOXC2+ paraxial tissue architecture.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Chirality destroys oriented active solids](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25953v1>)
*S. J. Kole, Gareth P. Alexander, Ananyo Maitra, Sriram Ramaswamy* <br>
Active chiral force densities generically destabilize three-dimensional uniaxial solids and isotropic chiral solids in anisotropic media, whereas higher-symmetry polar elastomers resist this instability and suppress leading-order chiral effects.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Effect of chirality on active elastomers and solids in three dimensions](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25945v1>)
*S. J. Kole, Gareth P. Alexander, Ananyo Maitra, Sriram Ramaswamy* <br>
High rotational symmetry strongly constrains chiral activity in active elastomers, whereas breaking this symmetry introduces force densities and odd elasticity that inherently destabilize the resulting uniaxial solids.
:::

:::
